current.text: He plays center on offense for Washington. Alex Sarr moves to power forward and switches on the perimeter.
Projected starters are Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Davis and Alex Sarr.
He and Trae Young are expected to get the top offensive touches in Washington, ahead of AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr.
Experts say he is healthy now and angling for a max contract.
He has looked good for the Wizards in the preseason.
He missed most of last season. One expert says part of that missed time in Washington was not true injury.
Experts do not expect 75 games. If he plays about 60 games, a mid-20s pick is a good one.
Experts see him as a top-20 per game player.
In recent mock drafts his draft spot has moved up. He now goes in the late second round more often, sometimes in the high teens.
Experts are comfortable taking him around picks 24 to 27, at the turn of rounds 2 and 3. He is a clear value at his Yahoo rank of 45. ESPN's rank of 14 is too high to draft him there.
In auctions, Josh values his per game line at 30 USD but would only buy him at a discount. He went for 26 USD in a mock auction.
Pairing him with Victor Wembanyama makes rebounds and blocks strong, but that team then needs guard stats.
Experts expect the Wizards to keep him, but a trade cannot be ruled out. The team could reconsider around the trade deadline.
Washington is trying to compete. The team is projected around 40 wins and in the play-in mix, so late-season rest and minutes cuts are not expected.
Washington has only 14 back-to-backs this season and one in the playoffs.

durable.text: Rebounds and blocks are his league-outlier categories. FG% and points are also clear strengths. He gives little in threes.
He has a long record of many different injuries, mostly lower body, plus shoulder and groin problems. In Dallas he never played five games in a row before getting hurt.
Experts disagree on how injury prone he is. Most call him injury prone. Lloyd notes that no single injury recurs, unlike repeated knee surgeries.
He is 33. His outside shooting and perimeter game decline every year, and he now rarely shoots except at the rim.
One expert says he can no longer shoot and is now a worse rim protector than Alex Sarr.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
As an often-injured player, he can be taken a bit earlier in roto than in head-to-head leagues.

note: He gives elite rebounds and blocks plus strong FG% and points, and costs little apart from threes. That makes him a strong frontcourt anchor for big-man builds, but the team then needs threes and guard stats. The price gap is wide: Yahoo values him at 23 USD (average cost 17.6 USD), ESPN at 45 USD (average cost 27.4 USD), and he went for 54 USD in our league last season. Experts treat him as a top-20 per game player who will miss games. A price around 26 to 30 USD is fair, and paying near the ESPN value or last year's price is not. Early in the season, check how often the Q (Rest) status costs him games and whether the Wizards still look like keeping him.
